summary: This Old House demonstrates an automatic leak-prevention system centered on a master emergency shutoff installed at the water main. A full-port ball valve closes the main line in response to detected moisture, stopping water flow to the entire house. Detection is modernized with a wireless network: a single wired connection from the valve to a hub and an RF/wifi-based array of puck sensors that can be placed around the home (near water heater, boiler, behind appliances, under sinks, etc.). When moisture is detected, a red alarm indicator pins the location of the triggered sensor, and the system shuts off water automatically; a manual override and reset are provided. Additional protection includes a low-temperature alarm suitable for basements to prevent freezing. The video emphasizes multiple common leak points (hoses, appliances) and positions sensors to cover those risk areas as an ounce of prevention against catastrophic water damage.

sections.description: The host outlines the threat of flooding from failed heaters, hoses, and appliances, and introduces a centralized master emergency shutoff positioned at the water main. The valve is a full-port ball valve capable of rapid closure in response to a sensor signal.

sections.title: System components: wireless sensors, hub, and placement strategy
concepts: one-wire connection from valve to hub
sections.description: The demonstration explains the transition from wired-only sensing to a wireless network. One wire runs from the valve to a central hub; a hub communicates with wireless puck sensors placed around the building in strategic locations (near water heater, boiler, behind washing machine, under sinks, etc.).

sections.title: Detection, alarm, shutoff, and reset workflow
concepts: red indicator points to the triggered sensor
sections.description: A leak is simulated by a small water drip; the system immediately sounds an alarm and shuts off the main supply. The operator can locate the cause via the red-flashing sensor indicator, then reset and restore water with a manual override if needed.
